name: Apache Doris
tagline: Real-time MPP analytical database with MySQL compatibility, search indexes and lakehouse access.
description: Apache Doris began as Baidu's Palo and is now an Apache top-level project: an MPP columnar database with a vectorized C++ engine, MySQL protocol compatibility and a simple two-component architecture (frontend and backend). It handles real-time ingestion with unique-key upserts, inverted indexes for log search, the VARIANT type for semi-structured data, vector indexes, and federated queries over Iceberg, Hudi, Paimon and Hive. A compute-storage separated mode runs on object storage. Doris overlaps heavily with StarRocks and ClickHouse; it is a good fit for real-time reporting and log analytics, with documentation and community still skewed toward China.

pricing.notes: Free to self-host; VeloDB sells a managed cloud and enterprise edition; Alibaba Cloud offers SelectDB/Doris services.

scale.notes: FE and BE nodes scale out; storage-compute separation mode stores data on object storage.

strengths: Simple architecture: just frontend and backend processes, no external coordinator
Inverted indexes and VARIANT type make it a credible log-analytics engine
Real-time upserts with unique-key model and partial column updates
Federated queries across Iceberg, Hudi, Paimon, Hive and JDBC sources
MySQL compatibility for tools and drivers
weaknesses: Feature overlap and divergence with StarRocks confuses evaluations
English docs and community are thinner than Chinese ones
Tuning bucketing and partitioning is still manual
notIdealFor: Teams needing a fully managed hyperscaler-native service
